identity.title: Learning to Discover Regulatory Elements for Gene Expression Prediction

problem.claim: Predict gene expression from DNA sequences while identifying the regulatory elements controlling expression.

contributions.claim: Seq2Exp explicitly discovers and extracts regulatory elements for target gene expression prediction.
The approach decomposes epigenomic signals and DNA sequences conditioned on causal active regulatory elements, then uses a Beta-distribution information bottleneck to filter non-causal components.
The source code is released in the AIRS library.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish Seq2Exp as a sequence-to-expression network explicitly designed to discover and extract regulatory elements.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that Seq2Exp outperforms existing baselines on gene expression prediction tasks.
The authors report that Seq2Exp discovers influential regions compared with MACS3, a commonly used statistical peak-detection method.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper frames gene expression prediction from DNA sequences and identifies regulatory-element discovery as a key challenge.
Seq2Exp is introduced to discover regulatory elements, model relationships among epigenomic signals, DNA sequences, and associated elements, and combine effects through a Beta information bottleneck.
Experiments compare Seq2Exp with prediction baselines and MACS3 for influential-region discovery.
Implementation is released through the AIRS library.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links the prediction task to explicit regulatory-element discovery and describes filtering non-causal components with an information bottleneck.

lessons.interpretation: A task-specific intermediate representation can align interpretability with the predictive objective.
lessons.application: For a structured prediction problem, define and evaluate an intermediate component tied to the target, then state how the model suppresses irrelevant components.
lessons.exception: This move may be unsuitable when no defensible intermediate structure exists or when filtering assumptions cannot be operationalized.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, metrics, improvement magnitudes, statistical significance, or experimental conditions.
It does not provide details sufficient to assess how causal relationships or influential-region discoveries were validated.
